mainTopic: Restoring רבי מאיר's name, and which kind of Torah scholar should lead: the one with vast knowledge, the sharp reasoner, or the one whose words cannot be refuted
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. רבי had been teaching his son a הלכה in the name of 'others', a code name for רבי מאיר, whose name was hidden because he had tried to remove the נשיא. The son trades פסוקים with his father and argues that since the plot failed, the name should not be hidden. רבי then quotes the teaching 'in the name of רבי מאיר', and רבא notes that even the humble רבי did not say 'רבי מאיר said'. Next, רבי יוחנן reports a מחלוקת over who is preferred: a סיני (a scholar with vast knowledge) or an עוקר הרים (a sharp reasoner). When this came up for real between רב יוסף and רבה, ארץ ישראל answered 'סיני', yet רב יוסף humbly let רבה lead for 22 years. The גמרא then tells how אביי became head of his learning group by making a statement no one could refute. It ends with a question about whether the sharp רבי זירא or the steady רבה בר רב מתנה is greater, which stays unresolved (תיקו). The amud closes with the הדרן that finishes פרק כהן משיח and all of מסכת הוריות.

steps.title: The son asks: why do we hide the names of these Sages?
steps.stepSummary: רבי finishes teaching his son a הלכה in the name of 'others,' and the son asks who these hidden Sages are.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...it would not be sacrificed.' The son said to him: Who are these people whose water we drink, but whose names we do not mention?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי has just finished teaching a הלכה in the name of 'others.' His son asks why they learn these Sages' Torah but never say their names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son points out something strange. We rely on these Sages' teachings ('drink their water'), yet we hide who they are. That seems ungrateful, so he asks who they are and why.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal someone tried to swap for a קרבן
Their water, a picture for their Torah teachings

phrases.english: it would not be sacrificed.
He said to him: Who are these
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי's son, רבן שמעון.

phrases.english: whose water we drink
but whose names we do not mention?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי הֵם הַלָּלוּ שֶׁמֵּימֵיהֶם אָנוּ שׁוֹתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the earlier part of the daf, where רבי מאיר's name was replaced with 'אחרים'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the unnamed Sages, and why their names are hidden.

steps.title: רבי explains: they tried to take away our family's honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that these Sages tried to remove the honor of his family, the family of the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They are people who tried to uproot your honor and the honor of your father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי explains why the names are hidden. These Sages tried to take away the honor of the נשיא's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiding their names was a response to their attempt to remove רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as נשיא. Because they tried to hurt the family's honor, their names were left out of the teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: Your father's house; your family line

phrases.english: He said to him: People
who sought to uproot your honor
and the honor of your father's house.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are the Sages who tried to remove the נשיא, so their names are kept hidden.

steps.title: The son quotes קהלת: they are dead, so let it go
steps.stepSummary: The son argues from a פסוק in קהלת that their feelings and conflict ended when they died.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Their love, their hatred, and their jealousy have already perished.'
steps.whatsHappening: The son pushes back on his father. He uses a פסוק to argue that these Sages have already died, so the old fight should be over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says that after people die, their love, hatred and jealousy are gone. The son uses this to argue there is no reason to keep punishing them by hiding their names.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'Their love,'
'their hatred, and their jealousy'
'have already perished'!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּם אַהֲבָתָם גַּם שִׂנְאָתָם גַּם קִנְאָתָם כְּבָר אָבָדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי gave for hiding the names.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's practice of keeping the names hidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Sages are dead and their feelings are gone, so the punishment should no longer apply.

steps.title: רבי answers from תהלים: the enemy is gone, but the damage stays
steps.stepSummary: רבי replies with a פסוק showing that even after the enemy is gone, the ruin they caused remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'The enemy has come to an end, but the ruins remain forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי defends his practice with a different פסוק. The people may be gone, but what they did still has effects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees the Sages are dead. But he argues that death does not erase the harm. Since the 'ruins' last, the response to them, hiding their names, can last too.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'The enemy has come to an end,'
'the ruins remain forever.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the son's פסוק with a counter-פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-verse showing that the effects of wrongdoing outlast the wrongdoer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the wrongdoers die, everything about the conflict is over.
steps.terutzMaskana: The harm they caused can remain even after they die, so the response can remain too.

steps.title: The son replies: their plan never worked
steps.stepSummary: The son says רבי's פסוק only applies when the enemies actually caused damage, and these Sages failed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies where their actions succeeded. But these Sages' actions did not succeed!
steps.whatsHappening: The son pushes back on his father's פסוק. That פסוק is about enemies who caused real ruin, but this plot failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son accepts the פסוק but limits it. 'Ruins remain forever' fits only when there really are ruins. Here the נשיא stayed in office, so there is no lasting damage to justify hiding the names.

phrases.english: He said to him: These words apply
where their actions were effective;
the Sages, their actions were not effective!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects how רבי applied the פסוק from תהלים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The application of 'the ruins remain forever' to this case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There are no 'ruins' here, because the plot to remove the נשיא failed.

steps.title: רבי is convinced and names רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי accepts his son's argument and repeats the teaching, now saying 'in the name of רבי מאיר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He then taught it to him again: They said in the name of רבי מאיר: If it were a תמורה, it would not be sacrificed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives in to his son. He teaches the same הלכה again, but this time he gives רבי מאיר's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה itself does not change. What changes is that רבי מאיר is now named openly instead of being called 'others.' The son's argument won.
steps.whatToRemember: The son convinced רבי that because the plot failed, there was no reason to keep hiding רבי מאיר's name. So רבי began quoting him by name.

phrases.english: He then taught him again,
They said in the name of רבי מאיר:
If it were a substitute,
it would not be sacrificed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אַתְנִי לֵיהּ אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the son's argument.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר's name is restored to his teachings.

steps.title: רבא praises רבי's humility
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that even the humble רבי said 'they said in the name of רבי מאיר' and not 'רבי מאיר said.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even רבי, who was humble, said 'They said in the name of רבי מאיר.' He did not say 'רבי מאיר said.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא comments on the exact wording רבי used. Even after agreeing, רבי did not quote רבי מאיר directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was famous for humility. Even so, he kept a small distance by saying 'they said in the name of' rather than the direct 'רבי מאיר said.' רבא points out that the old conflict still left a trace in the wording.

phrases.english: רבא said: Even רבי,
who is humble, (taught),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets ('taught') and some leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: 'They said in the name of רבי מאיר.'
He did not say 'רבי מאיר said.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי דְּעִנְוְותָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the exact wording רבי used in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the humble רבי quoted רבי מאיר only indirectly.

steps.title: Who is better: a scholar of vast knowledge or a sharp thinker?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן disagreed whether סיני or עוקר הרים is preferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן disagreed about this. One said: סיני is better. The other said: עוקר הרים is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about who should be given priority. Two types of scholar are compared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סיני knows a huge amount of Torah, as if it were all received at Sinai. An עוקר הרים is a brilliant reasoner who can 'uproot mountains' with sharp logic. The question is which one should come first, and the גמרא does not say which side held which view.

keyTerms.meaning: A scholar with vast, organized knowledge
An 'uprooter of mountains', a sharp, inventive thinker

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: They disagreed about this,
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the Rabbis,
one said: Sinai is preferable,
phrases.notes: 'Sinai' means someone who knows a huge amount, as if he had all the Torah from Sinai.

phrases.english: and one said: One who uproots mountains is preferable.
phrases.notes: Someone with such sharp reasoning that he can 'move mountains' in learning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן פְּלִיגוּ בַּהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to a new question about who gets priority among scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether a סיני or an עוקר הרים is preferred.

steps.title: A real case: רב יוסף versus רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף was a סיני and רבה an עוקר הרים, so the scholars of בבל asked ארץ ישראל which one comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף was a סיני; רבה was an עוקר הרים. They sent a question there: Which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this was a real, practical question. The scholars of בבל had to choose a head of the yeshiva and asked the Sages of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general question from the previous step now applies to two real people. One has vast knowledge and the other has sharp reasoning, so the community needs to know who should lead.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef was Sinai,
Rabba was one who uproots mountains.
They sent to there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל. The question was sent from בבל.

phrases.english: Which of them takes precedence?
phrases.notes: They were asking who should become head of the yeshiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general מחלוקת to a real case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the סיני (רב יוסף) or the עוקר הרים (רבה) should lead.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל answers: סיני comes first
steps.stepSummary: The answer was that סיני is preferred, because everyone needs the 'owner of the wheat.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent back to them: סיני is better, as the Master said: Everyone needs the owner of the wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages of ארץ ישראל answer that the scholar with vast knowledge comes first, and they give a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'owner of the wheat' is the one who has the raw material, meaning the sources themselves. Sharp reasoning needs sources to work with, so everyone ends up depending on the one who knows them.

keyTerms.meaning: Owner of the wheat, someone who holds the sources

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear principle for choosing a leader in Torah: mastery of the sources comes before sharp reasoning.

phrases.english: They sent to them: Sinai is preferable,
as the Master said:
Everyone needs the owner of the wheat,
phrases.notes: Just as everyone needs the one who has the wheat, everyone needs the one who knows the sources.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent from בבל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סיני comes first, because everyone depends on the one who holds the sources.

steps.title: רב יוסף steps aside and shows great humility
steps.stepSummary: Even so, רב יוסף refused the position. רבה led for 22 years, and in all that time רב יוסף acted with no air of authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רב יוסף did not accept it. רבה led for twenty-two years, and then רב יוסף led. And during all the years רבה led, רב יוסף did not even have a bloodletter come to his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the story. רב יוסף had the right to lead but stepped aside for רבה, and he stayed humble the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Though the ruling favored him, רב יוסף let רבה lead first and only became head after 22 years. He would not even call a bloodletter to his house, a small privilege of important people, so he would not seem to be acting like a leader.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not accept it upon himself

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling was that סיני (רב יוסף) comes first, but רב יוסף humbly let רבה lead for 22 years. He did not take even the smallest honor during that time.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ruling was ignored or overturned. סיני was still judged preferable. רב יוסף simply chose not to take the position.

phrases.english: And even so, did not accept
Rav Yosef [the position] upon himself.
Rabba reigned twenty-two years,
and then Rav Yosef reigned.
And all the years that Rabba reigned,
Rav Yosef, not even a bloodletter
did he call to his house.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, he went to the bloodletter himself instead of having him come over.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא קַבֵּיל רַב יוֹסֵף עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what actually happened after the ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: סיני is preferred, but רב יוסף humbly gave up the leadership to רבה and acted with no sign of authority.

steps.title: Four scholars set a test to choose their head
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רבא, רבי זירא and רבה בר מתנה needed a leader. They agreed that whoever said something that could not be refuted would be the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, רבא, רבי זירא and רבה בר מתנה were sitting and learning together, and they needed a head. They said: whoever says something that is not refuted will be the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story about four scholars choosing a leader. This step sets up the test, and the next step tells us the result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed whether a סיני or an עוקר הרים should lead. Here the group uses a simple practical test instead: whoever can make a statement that holds up against challenges will lead.

keyTerms.meaning: A head, meaning the leader of the group
A matter, a statement of Torah
Is refuted, gets knocked down by a challenge

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבָּה בַּר מַתְנָה
phrases.english: Abaye, Rava, Rabbi Zeira, and Rabba bar Mattana
were sitting, and they needed a head.
They said: Anyone who says a matter
and it is not refuted, let him be the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא וְרַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבָּה בַּר מַתְנָה הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of choosing a leader with a new story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The group will be led by whoever makes a statement that cannot be refuted.

steps.title: Only אביי passed the test and was told to begin teaching
steps.stepSummary: Everyone else's statements were refuted, but אביי's was not. רבה saw that אביי held his head high and told him: נחמני, begin and speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone's statements were refuted except אביי's. רבה saw that אביי lifted his head, and said to him: נחמני, begin and speak.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. אביי's statement held up, so he became the head, and רבה invited him to begin teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test from the last step worked: only one person's statement survived every challenge. רבה noticed from אביי's raised head that his words had not been refuted, and he called on him to lead the learning.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי became the head because his statement could not be refuted.

phrases.english: For everyone's statements were refuted,
but Abaye's was not refuted.
Rabba saw that Abaye raised his head,
phrases.notes: Lifting his head showed that his statement had held up.

phrases.english: He said to him: Nahmani, begin and speak.
phrases.notes: נחמני was אביי's real name. אביי was a nickname.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result of the test set up in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי passed the test and became the head of the group.

steps.title: Who is greater: the sharp questioner or the steady reasoner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is greater: רבי זירא, who is sharp and raises difficulties, or רבה בר רב מתנה, who is slow and steady but reaches conclusions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: between רבי זירא and רבה בר רב מתנה, which one is greater? רבי זירא is sharp and raises difficulties. רבה בר רב מתנה is slow and careful, and he reaches the conclusion. What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question comparing two different kinds of scholars. This step sets up the question, and the next step tells us how it ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each scholar has a different strength. One is quick and good at asking hard questions. The other is slower but brings the discussion to a final conclusion. The question is which strength is worth more.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the scholars)
Slow and careful, and reaches the conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר מתנה in step 12 and רבה בר רב מתנה here are the same person, written two slightly different ways.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב מַתְנָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabba bar Rav Mattana,
which of them is greater?
Rabbi Zeira is sharp and raises difficulties,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב מַתְנָה מָתוּן וּמַסֵּיק,
phrases.english: and Rabba bar Rav Mattana is slow and careful, and reaches the conclusion.
What is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises another question about which kind of scholar is greater, similar to the סיני versus עוקר הרים question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the sharp questioner (רבי זירא) or the steady reasoner who reaches conclusions (רבה בר רב מתנה) is greater.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question remains open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand. The question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not decide between the two scholars. It leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the סיני versus עוקר הרים question, which got a clear answer, this one stays undecided. Both kinds of strength are important, and the גמרא does not rank one above the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The question of רבי זירא versus רבה בר רב מתנה ends in תיקו, with no decision.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 14 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no decision about which of the two scholars is greater.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing כהן משיח and the end of מסכת הוריות
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק כהן משיח, which also ends the whole מסכת הוריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק כהן משיח, and מסכת הוריות is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line. It marks the end of the פרק and of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the discussion. It is a formula said when finishing a פרק, and here it also notes that the whole מסכת הוריות is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing formula of a פרק)

steps.whatToRemember: With this line, the פרק כהן משיח and all of מסכת הוריות are complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kohen Mashiah,
phrases.notes: כהן משיח is the name of this perek.

phrases.english: and Tractate Horayot is finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The formal closing after the last discussion of the פרק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק כהן משיח and מסכת הוריות are completed.
